title: Best Celebrity Halloween Costumes 2026: Paris Hilton as Britney, Lisa Rinna as Kylie & More】
body:
Hollywood’s elite turned the streets of Los Angeles and the red‑carpet‑styled parties into a runway of nostalgia, pop‑culture homage, and high‑glamour this Halloween, delivering a parade of costumes that sparked conversation on social media and set new standards for celebrity dress‑up. From Paris Hilton’s spot‑on Britney Spears tribute to Lisa Rinna’s playful Kylie Jenner ensemble, the night’s sartorial choices ranged from meticulously recreated on‑screen icons to tongue‑in‑cheek nods to fellow stars, underscoring how the holiday has become a platform for both personal expression and strategic publicity.

Paris Hilton, who has long cultivated a reputation as a trend‑setter, arrived at a private Halloween bash dressed as the pop queen who dominated the early 2000s. The look featured a glitter‑covered crop top, a low‑cut denim mini, and a signature blonde bob—complete with a replica of Britney’s iconic “…Baby One More Time” schoolgirl outfit for the opening segment of her costume. Fans praised the homage for its attention to detail, noting how Hilton’s version blended nostalgia with contemporary fashion cues, such as a modern, oversized bomber jacket that added a fresh twist. The choice also sparked a wave of online commentary about the resurgence of early‑2000s aesthetics in current streetwear, suggesting that Hilton’s costume may have inadvertently set a tone for the season’s broader style trends.

Equally buzz‑worthy was Lisa Rinna’s transformation into Kylie Jenner, complete with a meticulously crafted contouring makeup look, a faux‑fur coat reminiscent of Jenner’s 2023 Met Gala appearance, and a miniature, faux‑designer handbag. Rinna’s decision to embody a peer rather than a fictional character highlighted an emerging pattern among Hollywood’s A‑list: using Halloween as a stage to pay tribute to fellow influencers and amplify cross‑industry connections. Observers noted that the costume was not merely a playful mimicry but also a strategic nod to the power of social‑media branding, as Jenner’s own digital empire continues to shape modern celebrity culture.

Other notable entries included Camila Mendes, who revived her “Riverdale” alter ego Veronica Lodge with a sleek, black trench coat and a vintage leather satchel, and Madelaine Petsch, who channeled the 1990s grunge queen Courtney Love, complete with a ripped cardigan and a replica of Love’s signature “Hole” T‑shirt. Both actresses leveraged their iconic television roles to create instantly recognizable looks that resonated with fans who have followed their careers from teen dramas to mainstream stardom. Their choices underscore how Halloween serves as a bridge between an actor’s past performances and their current public persona, allowing them to reconnect with audiences on a nostalgic level while reinforcing brand continuity.

The event also saw a surge in costume choices that referenced classic cinema and cult favorites. Veteran star Michael B. Jordan arrived as Marty McFly from “Back to the Future,” complete with a self‑made hoverboard prop, while Zendaya opted for a sleek, futuristic version of the titular character from the 2025 sci‑fi thriller “Neon Dawn.” These selections reflect a broader industry trend where celebrities use Halloween to showcase their acting range and hint at upcoming projects, effectively turning a festive night into a low‑key promotional platform. Industry insiders suggest that such strategic costuming can generate early buzz for unreleased films, especially when the outfits are shared across the stars’ massive social‑media followings.

Beyond the individual outfits, the collective impact of these costumes points to an evolving Halloween culture within Hollywood. The night’s fashion choices were amplified by live streams, Instagram reels, and TikTok duets, turning private gatherings into global spectacles. Brands quickly capitalized on the moment, with several designers offering limited‑edition “celebrity‑inspired” pieces that mimicked the most talked‑about looks, thereby blurring the line between personal celebration and commercial opportunity. Analysts predict that this symbiotic relationship between celebrity costume choices and fashion retail will intensify, with future Halloween events likely to feature coordinated partnerships and exclusive product drops.

As the pumpkins are cleared and the glitter settles, the 2026 celebrity Halloween showcase has already set a benchmark for creativity, strategic branding, and cross‑industry homage. With social media continuing to magnify each sartorial decision, the next Halloween season promises even more elaborate collaborations, surprise references, and perhaps a deeper integration of upcoming film and television releases into the festivities. The convergence of nostalgia, pop‑culture reverence, and marketing savvy suggests that Halloween will remain a pivotal moment for Hollywood’s stars to both entertain and influence the cultural conversation.
